simple.meaning: חֶרְמֵשׁ (chermêsh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a sickle (as cutting).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֶרְמֵשׁ (H2770) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 16:9, with occurrences in Deuteronomy.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֶרְמֵשׁ (H2770) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֶרְמֵשׁ (H2770) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֶרְמֵשׁ (chermêsh) / H2770 is traced through Deuteronomy 16:9, Deuteronomy 23:26 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2770. chermesh חֶרְמֵשׁ noun [masculine] sickle (on form see Ges § 85 xii. 55) — Deut 16:9 ; Deuteronomy 23:26.

occurrences.englishText: You shall count for yourselves seven weeks. From the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
